children: Last week's unexpected increase in U.S. crude oil stockpiles as exports fell and refineries cut runs is "slightly bearish" for crude, but keeps upward pressure on gasoline prices, says David Russell of TradeStation. "Energy markets are tight but stabilizing," he says, "but it might be hard for crude to go much lower, given the record crack spreads." The EIA reported a 3 million barrel increase in crude oil stocks, leaving them 2% above the five-year average for the time of year, while gasoline inventories fell by 1.7 million barrels and were 6% below the average. WTI crude is up 2.1% at $92.41 a barrel after falling the previous five sessions. Nymex gasoline futures are up 1.4% at $3.5367 a gallon. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
